q: In physics, work is defined as the _____ product of the force applied and the displacement.
e: Work is defined as the scalar product of the force applied and the displacement, meaning it has magnitude but no direction.

q: The rate of doing work is defined as _____.
e: Power is specifically defined as the rate at which work is done or the rate of energy change.

q: The unit for power in SI units is the _____.
e: The SI unit for power is the watt (W), named after James Watt.

q: If the work done is 1 joule in 1 second, the power is _____.
e: By definition, 1 watt is equal to 1 joule of work done per 1 second.

q: In the CGS system, the unit of power is _____.
e: In the CGS system, power is measured in ergs per second (erg s$^{-1}$).

q: In the British engineering system, the unit of power is _____.
e: The British engineering system uses horse power (hp) as the unit of power.

q: 1 horse power is equal to _____ W.
e: The relationship between different units of power states that 1 hp = 746 W.

q: 1 horse power is equal to _____ ft-lb s$^{-1}$.
e: If the work done in 1 second is 550 ft-lb, the power is 1 horse power.

q: For uniform motion, power is equal to the product of force and _____.
e: For uniform motion, the rate of doing work or power is given by P = Fv, where v is average velocity.

q: The formula for power in terms of force and average velocity is _____.
e: Since work W = Fs and power P = W/t, substituting gives P = F(s/t) = Fv.

q: 1 W is equal to _____ erg s$^{-1}$.
e: The conversion between SI and CGS units of power is 1 W = $10^7$ erg s$^{-1}$.

q: The unit of power which is larger than watt and equals $10^6$ W is the _____.
e: 1 megawatt (MW) is equal to 1,000,000 W or $10^6$ W.
